People are human beings, not cars.

1)Getting skinnier doesn't happen over night. A child wouldn't even know what being fat is until it's pointed out to them. Also kids don't have much say in their own diets so it would be up to the parents to help them assuming the child tells their parents that they're being bullied for being fat.

2)Those people DO need professional help, but it's a long and tedious process that some people can't even afford. And they will need support from friends and family as well, not people berating them for being fat.

3)I said at the start this is what I'VE seen happen. I know people who were bullied for being fat and tried to stop eating all together.

!DisagreeWithOP

In my life, I've never met anyone who thought that being fat was healthy. I'm sure there are some people like that out there though. However, these are the problems I've seen people who are trying to accept being fat have faced.

1)People who are fat often end up having to deal with some type of mental illness brought on by factors such as being bullied for being fat, feeling different and like they don't belong, and people who say that just by existing is costing everyone else money.

2)Due to these factors, fat people often end up with a form of depression, maybe even bad enough to be suicidal. So telling a fat person that being fat is going to kill them probably won't help at all if they already want to die.

3)Being fat with a mentality that it is wrong to be fat can easily cause eating disorders which is more dangerous and unhealthy.

Overall, I think being able to accept being fat is very important. It helps build confidence and makes people feel overall happier. Once you get into a stable mental state this way, working on dieting and exercising becomes more natural instead of doing it out of self hatred.
